title: 2 Kings 12
paragraphs: ¹ Jehoash began to reign in the seventh year of Jehu and reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah of Beersheba. ² Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the years that Jehoiada the priest instructed him. ³ But the high places were not removed — the people continued to offer sacrifices and burn incense there. ⁴ Jehoash said to the priests, "Collect all the money brought as sacred offerings to the temple of the LORD — the census tax, the money received from personal vows, and any money that someone voluntarily brings to the temple. ⁵ Let the priests receive it, each from his own donors, and use it to repair whatever damage is found in the temple."

⁶ But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had still not repaired the temple. ⁷ Therefore King Jehoash called for Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and asked them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the temple? Stop accepting money from your donors and hand it over for the repair of the temple." ⁸ The priests agreed to stop accepting money from the people and to stop repairing the temple themselves. ⁹ Jehoiada the priest took a chest and bored a hole in its lid. He placed it to the right side of the altar as one enters the temple of the LORD. The priests who guarded the entrance put into it all the money brought to the temple. ¹⁰ Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the royal secretary and the high priest would count it and put it into bags.

¹¹ Then they would give the counted money to the men in charge of the work on the temple. They paid the carpenters and the builders who worked on the temple of the LORD, ¹² the masons and stone-cutters, and they bought timber and dressed stone to repair the temple, covering all the expenses of restoring it. ¹³ But the money brought into the temple was not used to make silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any other articles of gold or silver for the temple; ¹⁴ it was paid directly to the workers, who used it to repair the temple. ¹⁵ They did not require the men receiving the money to account for it, because they were acting in complete honesty.

¹⁶ The money from the guilt offerings and sin offerings was not brought into the temple of the LORD; it belonged to the priests. ¹⁷ About that time Hazael king of Syria went up and attacked Gath and captured it. Then he turned to march on Jerusalem. ¹⁸ Jehoash king of Judah gathered all the sacred objects that his predecessors — Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, kings of Judah — had dedicated, along with his own dedicated gifts and all the gold found in the treasuries of the temple of the LORD and the royal palace. He sent them all to Hazael king of Syria, who then withdrew from Jerusalem. ¹⁹ The rest of the events of Joash's reign and all his deeds are recorded in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah. ²⁰ His servants rose up and formed a conspiracy, and they killed Joash at Beth Millo on the road down to Silla.

²¹ It was Jozachar son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, who struck him down. He died and was buried with his ancestors in the city of David. And his son Amaziah succeeded him as king.
